objective: Prevent Community feed ad rows from disappearing during scrolling and allow unlimited comments with sparse optional interstitial ad opportunities beyond a conservative engagement threshold.
productionBaselineEvidence: GitHub main 5efb994 inspected 2026-11-11; PR #599 reports Nov 9 production OTA, but live binary and production source fingerprint have not been independently verified in this session.
rootCause: The Public and Org/Cluster Wall passed active=isAdActive(item.id). Inactive ad components rendered null before the list's 60%-visible/400-ms activation threshold, leaving a zero-height ad marker that fast scrolling could never activate.
chosenApproach: Always mount lightweight inline ad viewport probes on virtualized rows. Keep existing consent, current viewport, foreground, route, network, remote switches, NativeAd primary, Banner fallback, no-fill collapse, and request cooldown. Only confirmed extra comments queue a sparse optional interstitial for the next editor-close natural break.
selectedAlternativeReason: Avoid triggering ads for all offscreen posts or disabling ad safety gates. NativeAd cache or forced new requests per scroll would bypass cooldowns and increase waste.
preserveBehaviors: Existing Community video/audio and photo rendering
No third-party ad impressions fabricated; SDK only
Original backend comment RPC and server-side anti-farming/BP rules
A failed/missing ad never blocks user comments
No new ad unit, native build, Supabase schema or authorization changes
No unauthorized RC, production promotion or OTA publication
acceptanceChecks: Public and scoped feeds keep measurable ad probes before viewability
Only one confirmed-comment event is counted per successful RPC
Ad queued on sixth and each fifth further confirmed success; display only on editor-close if global cadence, consent and fill permit
User/day isolation and no client-side BP award
Existing Google and BUKLOD ads safety gates preserved
No native device or production fill claims without live test
deviceVerification: Pending. No actual Android device testing or production publishing authorized by this change.
